title: CO in the C1 globule of the Helix nebula with ALMA
question: Determine the physical properties (CO optical depth, isotopic ratios, molecular mass, tail origin) of the C1 cometary globule in the Helix nebula from 12CO, 13CO and C18O(2-1) emission

what.value: Observed 12CO/13CO ratio of ~10 for the entire nebula, used to estimate the 12CO optical depth

evidence.quote: Using the observed $^{12}$CO/$^{13}$CO ratio of $\sim$10 found by (cite: bachiller1997) for the entire nebula, we estimate the $^{12}$CO optical depth to be up to $\sim$10.

what.value: Dust temperature of the Helix nebula, 22 to 42 K, mean 30.8 +/- 1.4 K

evidence.quote: (cite: van2015) found that the temperature of the dust in the Helix nebula varies from $22$ to $42\,\textmd{K}$ with a mean value of $30.8\pm1.4\,\textmd{K}$.

what.value: Dust absorption coefficient K_d = 20 cm2/g for amorphous carbon at 1 mm and 20 K

evidence.quote: We use $K_\textmd{d}=20\,\,\textmd{cm}^2\,\textmd{g}^{-1}$ taken from (cite: mennella1998) for amorphous carbon dust grain at $1\,\textmd{mm}$ and at $20\,\textmd{K}$

what.value: CO/H abundance ratio ~3e-4 in the Helix nebula, giving the assumed CO/H2 = 6e-4

evidence.quote: assume a CO/H$_2$ ratio of 6$\,\times 10^{-4}$ based on the CO/H abundance ratio of $\sim$3$\,\times 10^{-4}$ in the Helix nebula in (cite: huggins1992; huggins2002)
Here we use $\chi_\textmd{d}=1\textmd{:}100$ as in (cite: meaburn1992).

what.value: AGB stellar model surface abundance ratios (solar Z=0.014 and Z=0.03) compared with the derived isotopic ratios

evidence.quote: The AGB models of (cite: Karakas2016) are used to compare these ratios with what is predicted by those models.

what.value: 12C/13C of presolar SiC grains for comparison

evidence.quote: We can also compare these predictions with observations of the $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C isotopic ratios of presolar grains in (cite: zinner2014).

what.value: 12C/13C (5 to 35) and 16O/18O (400 to 1250) ratios of SC-type AGB carbon stars for comparison

evidence.quote: The derived $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C ratio is within the range of the $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C ratios for different SC-type AGB carbon stars (C/O$\sim 1$) in (cite: abia2017), which range from 5 to 35.

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image the archival data
recipe.method: Manual CASA calibration of four measurement sets, combined, then tclean line cubes (multiscale) and continuum map (Hogbom)

recipe.goal: Measure integrated line spectra and fluxes
recipe.method: Integrated 12CO, 13CO and C18O spectra fitted with Gaussians to get peak, FWHM and total flux

recipe.goal: Derive excitation temperature and CO optical depths
recipe.method: Tex from the 12CO peak assuming optically thick 12CO; 13CO and C18O optical depth maps from Nishimura et al. formulae after converting intensity to brightness temperature via Rayleigh-Jeans; 12CO optical depth scaled from 13CO using a 12CO/13CO ratio of ~10
key_parameters: Masks at 3 sigma_13 (13CO) and 2 sigma_18 (C18O) on the integrated intensity maps
assumptions: LTE, a single excitation temperature for all three CO isotopologues, 12CO optically thick
12CO/13CO optical-depth ratio of ~10 taken from the literature

recipe.method: Ratio maps of integrated intensity with 13CO above 3 sigma at a common beam and pixel grid; ratio taken in the 12CO optically thin extended tail; converted with frequency^-3 relations; 16O/18O from 13CO/C18O ratio combined with the 12CO/13CO ratio
assumptions: Underlying 12C/13C isotopic ratio uniform across the globule

recipe.goal: Constrain progenitor mass using AGB models
recipe.method: Compare the derived isotopic ratios, and the 16O/18O to 12C/13C ratio, with Karakas (2016) model surface abundances at the end of the AGB
assumptions: Dust in the Helix is carbonaceous, requiring C/O > 1

recipe.goal: Derive molecular mass from 13CO and C18O column densities
recipe.method: J=2 column densities from optical depth maps, total column densities via partition function, scaled to 12CO by optical-depth-corrected isotopic ratios, converted to H2 mass at 201 pc

recipe.goal: Derive gas mass from 1.2 mm dust continuum
recipe.method: Total continuum flux density with a 2 sigma cut-off, converted to gas mass with a Rayleigh-Jeans optically thin dust formula
key_parameters: T_dust = mean 30.8 K; K_d = 20 cm2/g; dust-to-gas 1:100
assumptions: Free-free emission negligible; dust emission optically thin (gamma = 1)

recipe.method: Channel maps, declination velocity cuts and right ascension velocity cuts of 12CO and 13CO used to look for a head-to-tail velocity gradient expected from wind ablation (~10 km/s)
